correctness.rationale: The exact eight triples define 140 nonempty noncover faces with dimension counts (8,28,56,40,8). Exhausting all 40320 permutations gives 48 point automorphisms; their center is generated by z=(0 2)(1 3)(4 6)(5 7), and their induced action on the four pairs has order 24 and kernel ⟨z⟩. Independent exact rational row reduction gave boundary ranks 7,21,31,8 in degrees 1–4, hence reduced Betti numbers 4 in degree 2 and 1 in degree 3 only. Computing on a rational cycle-space quotient by the boundaries gives trace +1 on H̃₃ for all 48 elements. Signed simplicial Lefschetz traces then give χ₂(g)=sgn(ḡ)|Fix(ḡ)| element by element, where ḡ acts on the four pairs. Character equality over characteristic zero proves the rational module isomorphism, and decomposing the signed permutation module gives zero degree-two invariants, versus one in degree three. No incidence duality acts on the fixed side unless it preserves that side.
residual_risks: The verification concerns the explicit eight-point object and rational modules; it implies no integral equivariant splitting or general family theorem.

evidence: Bıyıkoğlu–Civan determine the underlying homotopy type on the graph, not its symmetry action. The distinct full-graph Resultary theorem specifies χ₄ as the side sign β and evaluates χ₃ for every graph automorphism; the fixed-side group is ker β of order 48.
broader_coverage.reasoning: After the demonstrated natural transfer, the full-graph theorem covers a strictly larger action, including side exchanges unavailable on the frozen vertex set. The older nonequivariant result alone would not be enough.

evidence: The four blocks can be recovered without a new symmetry calculation: each point has one other point on no common line. For each choice of three blocks the two lines using them are opposite choices from the blocks. A point permutation fixing all four blocks must thus flip either every pair or none. The order-48 side group has this order-two kernel, acts as S₄ on the blocks, and has center exactly that kernel.

In the full-graph character table χ₄=1 on ker β, so H̃₃ of the noncover complex is trivial. For the shifted four-dimensional character the two trace-4 elements exhaust its kernel, since a finite-order complex matrix of dimension four has trace 4 only when it is the identity. That kernel has order two, hence is central and is ⟨z⟩. Quotient 3-cycles lift to elements of orders 3 or 6, with trace 1; quotient 4-cycles lift to orders 4 or 8, with trace 0. Trace −2 occurs on exactly six quotient elements of order two, forcing them to be the transposition class rather than the three double transpositions. The latter have trace zero. These are precisely the character values of sgn⊗Q[the four pairs].
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The full statement, including the shifted degrees, central kernel and named rational representation, follows directly from the stronger result and the invariant cover. No separate equivariant invariant survives this comparison. The implication is independent of any claim as to which same-day record came first.

evidence: Number the first bipartition class by (u₀,u₂,u₄,u₆,v₁,v₃,v₅,v₇), in that order. The graph neighborhoods of vertices in the other class are exactly the eight frozen triples; since the neighborhoods are distinct, the side-preserving subgroup restricts isomorphically to the point group.

Let A be the simplex on the point class in the graph independence complex X, and B the union of the closed stars of the line vertices. The subcomplexes are invariant under the side-preserving group, X=A∪B, and A∩B is exactly the noncover complex. A is contractible; every nonempty indexed intersection of the line stars is the star of the corresponding line-vertex set, since no two line vertices are adjacent in the graph. These intersections are cones and the nerve is a full simplex, so B is contractible. The reduced Mayer–Vietoris connecting isomorphism H̃_{i+1}(X;Q)→H̃_i(A∩B;Q) is equivariant by naturality. There is no sign from interchanging the cover members, which are preserved individually.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The ordinary suspension equivalence in Tsukuda alone would not prove equality of characters. The invariant cover proves the needed module-level shift, with no need for equivariant contractibility. Thus the two targets are equivalent under side restriction and degree shift.

originality.rationale: The distinct Resultary record 8328b2388fb9 determines the complete homology character for all 96 automorphisms of the corresponding graph independence complex. Its restriction to the side-preserving subgroup, with homological degree lowered by one, gives the entire frozen rational character by a natural Mayer–Vietoris isomorphism. The explicit transfer below resolves the apparent difference between the two complexes; it is not an inference from matching trace histograms or from the shared date. The records have the same catalogue date, so their order of publication or discovery is not determined here.
residual_risks: Neither the shared date nor this mathematical coverage comparison determines discovery, publication priority, or attribution. The statement-level implication is decisive regardless of that chronology.

value.rationale: A full rational character for this configuration would be a natural valuable invariant if unknown. Here it is the fixed-side restriction of the independently indexed full graph character under a standard natural connecting isomorphism. The explicit enumeration is useful as corroboration, but it does not supply a distinct scientific result beyond that coverage. The block description and invariants are immediate once the restriction is recognized; no independently valuable narrower claim remains to repair.
residual_risks: This does not assess new integral representation calculations or genuine equivariant homotopy classifications, neither of which is claimed in the frozen record.
